argument_summary: The certification request is supportable only on a narrow, caveated basis. The admissible record shows aggregate readiness cleared by 2.4 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a monitored 3% rollout with rollback capability. That supports launch readiness in a risk-managed sense, but not a claim that rollout controls cured the known weakness. The same admissible record also shows the health-plan benefits support segment remains below target and exposed in the initial cohort, while the available risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not cover that exposure. The correct packet is therefore certification with explicit disclosure of that material limitation, not escalation based on an overbroad reading that certification necessarily implies the weakness was resolved.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not permit treating a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage as a substitute for disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed. The admissible policy record instead supports a narrower position: certification can proceed only if the packet and model-card record expressly disclose the material limitation for the named launch use case, because the issue is neither resolved nor covered by approved risk acceptance. Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management is consistent with that approach because it favors explicit disclosure of limitations and evaluation results alongside deployment monitoring.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit concern. Remaining uncertainty can be handled through caveated compliance because the launch is already bounded by monitored, reversible rollout controls, so escalation is unnecessary if the certification record is narrowed and the disclosure requirement is made explicit.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support segment is below target on benefits-eligibility explanation.
That weak segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort because the tenant-randomized gate does not exclude it.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
Rollout controls alone do not satisfy the disclosure requirement under the stated policy.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel content is relied on as public support.
